s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of disorganized speech, anxiety, and self-harm behaviors with rapid progression of cognitive decline and psychiatric symptoms
salient_findings: Abrupt onset of disorganized speech and self-harm behaviors
Rapid, fluent, and nonsensical speech
Development of agitation, persecutory delusions, and hallucinations
Urinary and fecal incontinence
Significant cognitive impairment with disorientation and poor performance on cognitive tests
key_facts: 74-year-old right-handed woman
5-month history of symptoms
Symptoms began after a family trip
History of depression treated with sertraline
No prior cognitive impairment or neurological disease
Disoriented to time
Anomia and perseveration on cognitive tests
Impaired performance on Luria’s three-step test and defective crossed-pentagon drawing
MMSE score of 2/30 and ACE-R score of 2/100
Initial brain MRI reported as normal
Started on memantine and quetiapine without clinical improvement

shortlist.label: Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease
shortlist.why_kept: Rapid progression of cognitive decline and psychiatric symptoms

shortlist.label: Frontotemporal dementia
shortlist.why_kept: Acute onset of disorganized speech, anxiety, and self-harm behaviors with prominent frontal and temporal features

shortlist.label: Autoimmune encephalitis
shortlist.why_kept: Acute onset of symptoms, psychiatric symptoms, and lack of prior cognitive impairment or neurological disease

shortlist.label: Lewy body dementia
shortlist.why_kept: Cognitive decline, psychiatric symptoms, and visual hallucinations

shortlist.label: Alzheimer's disease
shortlist.why_kept: Cognitive decline and disorientation, although the acute presentation is atypical

raw.rationale: The patient's rapid onset of severe cognitive decline, disorganized speech, and prominent neurological features such as myoclonus are not explicitly mentioned but the rapid progression and combination of cognitive, psychiatric, and neurological symptoms are more consistent with Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease, especially given the lack of prior cognitive impairment or neurological disease and the absence of significant improvement with standard dementia treatments.

rejected.label: Frontotemporal dementia
rejected.why: Typically presents with more gradual decline and prominent changes in personality or language early in the disease course

rejected.label: Autoimmune encephalitis
rejected.why: Would likely have more prominent inflammatory markers or response to immunotherapy, which is not mentioned

rejected.label: Lewy body dementia
rejected.why: Characterized by fluctuations in cognitive function, visual hallucinations, and parkinsonian motor symptoms, which are not the primary features here

rejected.label: Alzheimer's disease
rejected.why: Unlikely given the acute onset and rapid progression of symptoms, as well as the lack of response to standard Alzheimer's treatments
